molecularGastronomyGuide.title: Molecular Gastronomy: Exploring the Science of Flavor
molecularGastronomyGuide.author: Hervé This
molecularGastronomyGuide.description: Discover the chemistry behind cooking techniques and flavor transformations
molecularGastronomyGuide.introduction: Molecular gastronomy explores the physical and chemical transformations that occur during cooking. Understanding these processes enables precision, innovation, and deeper appreciation of food.

fundamentalConcepts.name: The Maillard Reaction
fundamentalConcepts.description: Chemical browning that creates complex flavors and aromas
process: Amino acids and sugars react at high temperature
Creates hundreds of new flavor compounds
Produces brown color (melanoidins)
Generates appealing aromas
optimization: High heat is essential (don't crowd pan)
Allow proper time for browning (5-7 minutes per side)
fundamentalConcepts.commonMistake: Covering the pan traps steam, preventing browning

fundamentalConcepts.name: Caramelization
fundamentalConcepts.description: Breaking down sugars through heat to create sweet and bitter compounds
fundamentalConcepts.chemicalBreakdown: C12H22O11 (Sucrose) → Complex polymers and flavor compounds
tips: Use stainless steel pan (dark pans hide color changes)
Have cream ready to add (it will bubble)
Work quickly once sugar starts melting
Stop heating before reaching desired color - residual heat continues cooking

fundamentalConcepts.name: Emulsification
fundamentalConcepts.description: Combining ingredients that normally don't mix (oil and water)
fundamentalConcepts.principle: Emulsifiers have both hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends

breakingProblems.solution: Keep all ingredients at same temperature
Add oil drop-by-drop at first, then slowly increase speed
Stop when fully emulsified; continued beating breaks emulsion

fundamentalConcepts.rescue: If emulsion breaks, start with fresh egg yolk in new bowl, slowly whisk in broken emulsion

fundamentalConcepts.name: Gelation
fundamentalConcepts.description: Creating gel-like structures by trapping liquid in a protein or carbohydrate network

methods.process: Protein strands form 3D network as temperature drops
methods.uses: Aspics, panna cotta, fruit gels, savory mousses

methods.process: Carbohydrate chains form network at 40°C during cooling
methods.meltPoint: 85°C (185°F) - must be heated to break gel
methods.uses: Spheres, noodles, firm gels that don't melt easily

methods.process: Requires sugar (55%+) and acid (pH < 3.5) for gelation
methods.acidNeeded: Lemon juice, vinegar, or food acid

methods.process: Starch granules swell with heat, thickening liquid
methods.notes: Creates opaque, thick gels; not clear

spherification.definition: Creating liquid-filled spheres using sodium alginate and calcium chloride
process: Sodium alginate solution forms outer skin
Calcium chloride causes gelation at contact point
Results in thin membrane holding liquid inside

fundamentalConcepts.name: Foams and Airs
fundamentalConcepts.description: Trapping gas bubbles in liquid or protein networks to create light, airy textures

foamTypes.method: Immersion blender with soy lecithin solution
process: Add 0.5-1% soy lecithin to flavorful liquid
Heat until warm
Use immersion blender to create air bubbles
Skim foam from surface

foamTypes.method: Whisking liquid with gelatin to capture air
foamTypes.stabilizer: Gelatin proteins in partially set state
foamTypes.stability: High - holds shape for extended period

fundamentalConcepts.foamScience: Bubbles are surrounded by thin film of liquid/protein that prevents collapse

fundamentalConcepts.name: Spherification
fundamentalConcepts.description: Creating caviar-like spheres or larger encapsulated flavors

process: Dissolve 1% sodium alginate in flavorful liquid
Prepare calcium chloride bath (0.5-1% concentration)
Drop alginate mixture into bath using syringe/spoon
Allow 30 seconds to form skin
Remove with slotted spoon
Rinse in clean water

reverseSpherification.use: For acidic liquids (citrus, vinegar) that prevent alginate gelation
reverseSpherification.process: Reverse roles - calcium in liquid, sodium alginate bath

troubleshooting.solution: Increase alginate %, adjust pH, or use reverse spherification

temperatureControlTechniques.name: Sous Vide (Vacuum Sealing and Slow Cooking)
process: Vacuum seal food in plastic pouch
Submerge in temperature-controlled water bath
Cook for extended period (30 minutes to 24+ hours)
Finish with high-heat sear for crust (optional)
advantages: Exact doneness from edge to center
examples: Pulled pork and braises over 12+ hours
temperatureControlTechniques.science: Low heat gently denatures proteins without squeezing out moisture

temperatureControlTechniques.name: Reverse Searing
temperatureControlTechniques.temperature: Low then high (140-175°C oven, then pan sear)
process: Cook meat low and slow in oven (140-175°C/285-350°F)
Until internal temp reaches target (5°C below final)
Rest 10 minutes
Sear in screaming hot pan (30 seconds per side)
Rest again
temperatureControlTechniques.advantage: Even cooking from edge to center, then perfect crust

temperatureControlTechniques.name: Spherification in Water Bath
temperatureControlTechniques.temperature: Controlled room temperature or warmed bath
warmBath: Warmer bath speeds gelation (faster membrane formation)
Cooler bath slows gelation (thinner, more tender membrane)

chemicalTransformations.name: Protein Denaturation
chemicalTransformations.description: Heat causes protein structures to unfold and re-bind, changing texture
chemicalTransformations.process: Heat disrupts hydrogen bonds holding protein shape
consequences: Can squeeze out moisture if overcooked
examples: Raw fish muscle → cooked fish flakes apart
Meat proteins crosslink, squeezing moisture (overcooked = dry)
controllingDenaturation: Low temperature = gentle denaturation without moisture loss
Medium temperature = balanced texture and moisture
High temperature = rapid denaturation, potential drying

chemicalTransformations.name: Starch Gelatinization
chemicalTransformations.description: Starch granules absorb water and swell with heat
process: Starch granules are insoluble in cold water
With heat and water, granules absorb moisture
Swell to 10x original size
Thicken surrounding liquid
examples: Flour-thickened sauce becoming opaque and thick
Rice grains swelling and softening during cooking
chemicalTransformations.caution: Excessive heat can break down starch structure, causing thinning

chemicalTransformations.name: Fat Oxidation and Rancidity
chemicalTransformations.description: Fats break down through oxidation, creating off-flavors
prevention: Store oils in cool, dark place
Avoid repeated heating of same oil
Use oils appropriate for cooking temperature
Don't expose to metal containers (except stainless steel)
smokePoints: Extra virgin olive oil: 160°C (320°F) - finish, don't cook

flavorCompounds.name: Volatile Compounds (Aromas)
flavorCompounds.description: Small molecules that evaporate and create smell/taste

examples.best_at: Fresh or briefly heated (heat destroys fresh aroma)
Raw or briefly cooked (extended heat mellows harshness)

flavorCompounds.cooking_timing: Add volatile-heavy herbs at end of cooking to preserve aromas

flavorCompounds.name: Non-Volatile Flavor Compounds
flavorCompounds.description: Larger molecules that contribute taste but don't evaporate

examples.sources: Aged parmesan, tomatoes, mushrooms, fermented foods

examples.note: Can be reduced by long cooking or dilution

steps: Start with emulsifier at room temperature (egg yolk, mustard, butter)
Slowly drizzle in fat (oil or melted butter)
Initially add fat drop-by-drop while whisking constantly
Once emulsion starts forming, can add fat in thin stream
If it breaks, start fresh emulsifier and slowly whisk in broken sauce
practicalApplications.science: Emulsifier molecules arrange at oil/water interface, preventing separation

practicalApplications.method: Use meat thermometer inserted into thickest part, away from bone
practicalApplications.rest: Always rest 5-10 minutes after cooking (temperature equalizes, juices redistribute)

practicalApplications.timing: Start with brown vegetables, add tomato paste (caramelize), add stock, long simmer
